connections.why: Electron arrangement of an atom determines its position in the periodic table
An element's group predicts whether it bonds ionically, covalently or metallically
The type of bond and structure explains a substance's melting point, conductivity and strength
Diamond, graphite and fullerenes show how carbon's bonding dictates very different properties
Nanoparticle behaviour follows from how surface bonding scales with particle size
Conservation of mass underpins using moles to calculate reacting masses
Mole calculations give the theoretical yield against which actual yield and atom economy are judged
Reactivity trends down and across the table set up the metal reactivity series
Metals too reactive to extract by reduction with carbon are obtained by electrolysis
Electrolysis works because ionic compounds contain mobile, oppositely charged ions
Neutralisation titrations apply mole and concentration calculations
The energy released by exothermic reactions is harnessed as voltage in cells
The reactivity difference between two metals determines a simple cell's voltage
Activation energy links the energy profile of a reaction to how fast it goes
Equilibrium is reached when forward and reverse reaction rates become equal
The Haber process is the classic industrial equilibrium optimised for yield and rate
Combustion of hydrocarbon fuels is the main source of atmospheric pollutants
Alkene monomers join by addition polymerisation to make synthetic polymers
Changes in atmospheric carbon dioxide drive the greenhouse effect and climate change
Finite resources motivate life-cycle assessment and recycling to reduce impact
